shared_elements: monolithic stone block with a broad upper section over a narrower shaft
shallow low-relief carving on coarse, weathered stone
animal or creature heads/bodies in profile
vertically stacked registers or zones of decoration
row of repeated vertical/arched motifs across the upper area
sinuous, snake-like curvilinear forms in a lower zone
small subsidiary figures set within a larger field
justification: Both are monumental stone blocks with a wide top over a narrower body, carved in the same shallow, simplified, outline-driven relief and organised into stacked zones: repeated vertical/arched motifs across the upper part, profile creatures in the middle, and sinuous serpentine curves toward the base. The clearest difference is legibility and format \u2014 A's flat T-shaped slab presents crisp, well-separated animal figures and a distinct banded zigzag register, while B's rounded, three-dimensional, heavily eroded body carries denser, more ambiguous vertical elements that read as a continuous wrapped surface rather than discrete framed panels.
